pairs.why: Both feeders have similar soft-edged, outline-free wood; B's metal rivets and ring add small hard-edged detail, but the real feeder has few such edges, so the edges give no clear reason to choose.
A's chunky locker has soft, rounded edges and simple louvers, like the real one; B has similar edges but more hairline seams and a thin door gap.
A's keys are cream-and-cyan blocks with crisp but outline-free edges and a visible gap between keys, closer to the real labeled keys than B's dark keys that blend into the body with lost edges.
A's hull and sails have soft, fairly clean edges like the real ship; B has more thin rigging lines, ladders and foam edges, so it is busier.
A's cap has a soft white crown and a clean edge, and the lines on it are few, as on the real cap; B's rim is hard and glossy with highlight edges, and its dark wood background is busier.
A's rope and cross-bar have clean, soft edges like the real anchor, while B's ring and balls have a slightly harder contour.
A's pale stone has soft edges with a few fine crack lines, like the real stone, while B's chess squares and base are more crisp.
A's labeled buttons make a clean edge hierarchy like the real card, while B's unlabeled dark keys on a dark body leave lost edges and an uneven panel.
